summary: Streaming generation ends suddenly for very large max_tokens after GPU preemption in Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that streaming completions stop mid-generation when requesting very large max_tokens (e.g., 120k+). The behaviour appears during sustained long-context sessions on Dedicated capacity: initial streaming proceeds for a large portion of the request, then the stream breaks with no finalization chunk and client sees connection closed / 499-style client disconnects. Impact: customer sessions time out, partial outputs lost; affects production inference for a cohort of learning content generation jobs.

Impact:
- A subset (~8%) of long-running generations for NovaEdu in prod-us-east terminate before finalization.
- Observable as abrupt stream termination; downstream jobs re-run and costs spike.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ddg-dedicated-us-east-3
- Service: Redwood hosted inference (dedicated)
- Approx traffic spike window: 2026-03-01T14:05:00Z - ongoing

Observed behaviour:
- Streaming websocket/HTTP chunked responses stop sending final token chunks.
- Server logs show GPU preemption/host reassignment around same time as stream drop.
- KV-cache eviction events and a ‘session-preempt’ scheduler log entry appear seconds before the cutoff.

Expected behaviour:
- Long generation completes with finalization chunk or graceful fallback to a compatible model variant; no abrupt stream close.

Attachments: request IDs, sampling of logs and trace links provided below.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use customer account (NovaEdu dedicated pool).
2) Submit a streaming generation request against redwood/open-65b-qat with max_tokens set to ~120000 and a 200k-context prepended prompt (system + long doc).
3) Observe streaming chunks for ~10-30 minutes.
4) Note abrupt stream termination without finalization chunk and absence of retry from client side.
5) Cross-check serving runtime and autoscaler logs for that request_id.

Note: reproduction reliably seen when autoscaler triggers node preemption during long-running requests.
logs:
Sample correlated log snippet (timestamps UTC):
- 2026-03-01T14:12:02Z request_id=req-88a2f6a3 stream_chunk=token_seq_12000
- 2026-03-01T14:12:45Z node=ddg-node-11 gpu_state=ACTIVE memory_usage=82% kv_cache_size=98MB
- 2026-03-01T14:12:47Z autoscaler:scale_down_decision pool=ddg-dedicated-us-east-3 target=10->9 reason=balancer_idle
- 2026-03-01T14:12:48Z scheduler:preempt session=req-88a2f6a3 node=ddg-node-11 preempt_initiator=autoscaler
- 2026-03-01T14:12:49Z runtime:kv_cache:evict key=prefix-req-88a2f6a3 reason=node-shutdown
- 2026-03-01T14:12:50Z stream:connection_closed code=1001 reason="node shutdown" request_id=req-88a2f6a3
- 2026-03-01T14:12:51Z client=NovaEdu-worker-5 observed=stream_terminated_no_finalizer

Trace links: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/req-88a2f6a3
System logs show the preemption event coincident with eviction and stream termination.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler-triggered preemption causes in-flight session to be migrated; during migration the runtime evicts KV cache for that session and the streaming finalizer queue loses context resulting in abrupt close.

What we've validated so far: 
- Reproduced in staging by forcing node preemption during a long generation; same signature: autoscaler preempt -> KV eviction -> stream terminates without finalization sent.
- When we block autoscaler from draining nodes, the long-stream completes normally (baseline).
- Observed race between finalizer flush routine and node shutdown handler: finalizer tries to push final chunk but underlying socket closed by shutdown sequence.
- No application-level 5xx returned; the client observes connection close and treats as timeout.

Open questions: 
- Why is session migration not attempting a graceful fallback to another node or model variant?
- Whether KV cache snapshot/transfer is attempted (we see eviction rather than snapshot).

Telemetry artifacts: priority traces, heap profiles during preemption, autoscaler decision logs and node drain timing correlate to timeouts.
comments: Support (2026-03-01 15:10 UTC) - Ava Patel: Acknowledged from support. Assigned to SRE for priority investigation. Apologized and requested request_ids and example payloads.

SRE (2026-03-01 18:42 UTC) - Martin O'Neill: Reproduced in staging by initiating scale-down during an active long-generation. Confirmed forced node preemption closes socket before finalizer completes. Opening INT ticket to modify drain behavior.
Customer (2026-03-02 02:05 UTC) - NovaEdu Ops: Provided 6 failing request_ids and said this impacts nightly course generation jobs causing retries and cost spike. Asked for ETA on workaround.

SRE (2026-03-03 09:30 UTC) - Martin O'Neill: Implemented temporary mitigation: blocked scale-down on ddg-dedicated-us-east-3 for 48 hours and enabled extended pre-drain window for sessions >30 minutes. Observed no further terminations in that window. Planning a code fix for safer in-flight migration.
Support (2026-03-04 08:12 UTC) - Ava Patel: Notified customer of temporary mitigation and ongoing patch work; requested permission to keep extended pre-drain enabled until patch is rolled out.
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigation: Disabled autoscaler scale-down for affected pool and increased node pre-drain grace period for sessions >30 minutes; customer confirmed reduced incidence.

Planned permanent fix (work in progress):
- Modify scheduler to mark long-running streaming sessions as non-preemptible or to trigger graceful handoff with KV-cache snapshot/transfer.
- Add a finalizer flush checkpoint that persists final chunk to durable storage if socket closes during node shutdown, enabling resume or graceful retry.
- PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4528 (adds pre-drain anchors and KV snapshot path).

Follow-up items:
- Engineering to validate KV snapshot performance overhead on throughput.
- Product to update runbook for Dedicated customers on best practices for ultra-long generations.

Status: Mitigation in place; permanent fix targeted for the next minor release (v1.23.4) and tested in staging.
